sentences.zh: 王奐

translations.literal: Wang Huan
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan

sentences.zh: 王奐字彥孫，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Huan, style name Yansun, was a native of Linyi in Langya Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan, whose style name was Yansun, came from Linyi in Langya Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖僧朗，宋左光祿、儀同。

translations.literal: His grandfather Senglang served in Song as Left Director of the Imperial Secretariat with the same ceremonial rank as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Senglang had been Left Director of the Imperial Secretariat in the Song, with commissioner rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 父粹，黃門郎。

translations.literal: His father Cui was a Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cui had served as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 奐出繼從祖中書令球，故字彥孫。

translations.literal: Huan was adopted out to succeed his father's cousin, the Secretariat Director Qiu; hence his style name Yansun.
translations.idiomatic: Huan had been given in adoption to succeed his father's cousin Qiu, Secretariat Director, and therefore took the style name Yansun.

sentences.zh: 解褐著作佐郎，太子舍人，安陸王冠軍主簿，太子洗馬，本州別駕，中書郎，桂陽王司空諮議，黃門郎。

translations.literal: Upon leaving coarse cloth he became Assistant Editor in the Secretariat, Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household, chief clerk to the Champion General of Prince Anlu, Groom in the Heir Apparent's Household, provincial aide of his native commandery, Secretariat Gentleman, adviser to the Minister of Works for Prince Guiyang, and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Upon taking his first office he served successively as Assistant Editor in the Secretariat, Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household, chief clerk to the Champion General in Prince Anlu's household, Groom in the Heir Apparent's Household, provincial aide in his home commandery, Secretariat Gentleman, adviser to the Minister of Works for Prince Guiyang, and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 元徽元年，爲晉熙王征虜長史、江夏內史，遷侍中，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhui he became chief administrator to the General Who Subdues the Barbarians for Prince of Jinxi and Interior Administrator of Jiangxia, then was promoted to Palace Attendant and concurrently Colonel of the Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yuanhui era he was made chief administrator to the General Who Subdues the Barbarians for the Prince of Jinxi and Interior Administrator of Jiangxia, then promoted to Palace Attendant while retaining the post of Colonel of the Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 復出爲晉熙王鎮西長史，加冠軍將軍、江夏武昌太守。

translations.literal: He went out again as chief administrator to the General Who Guards the West for Prince of Jinxi, with the additional titles General Who Establishes Valor and Grand Administrator of Jiangxia and Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was again sent out as chief administrator to the General Who Guards the West for the Prince of Jinxi, with the additional rank of General Who Establishes Valor and the posts of Grand Administrator of Jiangxia and Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 徵祠部尚書，轉掌吏部。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of the Imperial Clan and then transferred to head the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Minister of the Imperial Clan and then put in charge of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 昇明初，遷冠軍將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shengming he was moved to General Who Establishes Valor and Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shengming era he was transferred to General Who Establishes Valor and Intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 初，王晏父普曜爲沈攸之長史，常慮攸之舉事，不得還。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Yan's father Puyao had been chief administrator to Shen Youzhi and had constantly feared that Youzhi would raise troops and that he would not be able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Yan's father Puyao had served as chief administrator to Shen Youzhi and had long worried that Youzhi would rebel and that he would never get home.

sentences.zh: 時奐爲吏部，轉普曜爲內職，晏深德之。

translations.literal: At that time Huan was in the Ministry of Personnel and transferred Puyao to an inner-office post; Yan was deeply grateful.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan headed the Ministry of Personnel he transferred Puyao to a capital post, for which Yan felt deep gratitude.

sentences.zh: 及晏仕世祖府，奐從弟蘊反，世祖謂晏曰：「王奐宋家外戚，王蘊親同逆黨，旣其羣從，豈能無異意。

translations.literal: When Yan entered service in the heir's household of Emperor Shizu, Huan's cousin Yun rebelled. Shizu said to Yan: "Wang Huan is a maternal kinsman of the Song house; Wang Yun is kin to the rebel faction. Since they are of the same clan, how could there be no divergent intent?
translations.idiomatic: When Yan took office in Emperor Shizu's princely household, Huan's cousin Yun rose in rebellion. Shizu said to Yan, "Wang Huan is a Song imperial in-law, and Wang Yun is close kin to the rebels. Men of the same clan—how can they not harbor divided loyalties?

sentences.zh: 我欲具以啓聞。」

translations.literal: I wish to report the whole matter fully."
translations.idiomatic: I intend to lay the whole matter before the throne."

sentences.zh: 晏叩頭曰：「王奐脩謹，保無異志。

translations.literal: Yan kowtowed and said: "Wang Huan is cultivated and cautious; I guarantee he has no divergent intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yan kowtowed and said, "Wang Huan is scrupulous and restrained; I warrant that he harbors no disloyal intent.

sentences.zh: 晏父母在都，請以爲質。」

translations.literal: Yan's parents are in the capital; I ask that they be held as hostages."
translations.idiomatic: My parents are in the capital—let them stand as hostages for him."

sentences.zh: 世祖乃止。

translations.literal: Shizu then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu thereupon dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 出爲吳興太守，秩中二千石，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He went out as Grand Administrator of Wuxing, with salary of two thousand piculs at the middle grade; his generalship was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Grand Administrator of Wuxing at the middle two-thousand-picul rank, retaining his general's title.

sentences.zh: 尋進號征虜將軍，

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter his designation was advanced to General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his designation was raised to General Who Subdues the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，進號左將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, his designation was advanced to General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyuan, he was then advanced in rank to General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷太常，領鄱陽王師，仍轉侍中，祕書監，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: The next year he was moved to Minister of Ceremonies and concurrently tutor to the Prince of Poyang, then transferred to Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, and concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Minister of Ceremonies and tutor to the Prince of Poyang, then moved to Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat while retaining the post of General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 又遷征虜將軍、臨川王鎮西長史、領南蠻校尉、南郡內史。

translations.literal: He was again moved to General Who Subdues the Barbarians, chief administrator to the General Who Guards the West for Prince of Linchuan, and concurrently Colonel of the Southern Barbarians and Interior Administrator of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to General Who Subdues the Barbarians, chief administrator to the General Who Guards the West for the Prince of Linchuan, and concurrently Colonel of the Southern Barbarians and Interior Administrator of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 奐一歲三遷，上表固讓南蠻曰：「今天地初辟，萬物載新，荊蠻來威，巴濮不擾。

translations.literal: Huan was transferred three times in one year. He submitted a memorial firmly declining the Southern Barbarians post, saying: "Now heaven and earth have just been opened anew and the myriad things bear fresh life; the Jing barbarians have come to submit and Ba and Pu are undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Huan changed posts three times in a single year. He submitted a memorial firmly declining the post of Colonel of the Southern Barbarians, writing, "Heaven and earth have only just been renewed and all things put on a fresh footing; the barbarians of Jing have submitted, and Ba and Pu are untroubled.

sentences.zh: 但使邊民樂業，有司脩務，本府舊州，日就殷阜。

translations.literal: If only the border people are made content in their occupations and the responsible offices attend to their duties, this former province of our headquarters daily grows prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: If the border people are left to prosper in their work and the responsible offices carry out their duties, this old provincial seat of our headquarters grows more prosperous by the day.

sentences.zh: 臣昔遊西土，較見盈虛，兼日者戎燼之後，痍毀難復。

translations.literal: Your servant once traveled in the western lands and has closely seen fullness and emptiness; moreover, since the recent aftermath of military fires, wounds and ruin are hard to restore.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant once traveled in the western regions and saw for himself how prosperity and ruin alternate; and since the recent wars, the devastation has been so severe that recovery is still difficult.

sentences.zh: 雖復緝以善政，未及來蘇。

translations.literal: Even if good government is applied to gather things together, it has not yet reached the point of returning life.
translations.idiomatic: Even with good government binding the wounds, the land has not yet returned to life.

sentences.zh: 今復割撤大府，制置偏校，崇望不足以助強，語實安能以相弊？

translations.literal: Now to cut away again from the great headquarters and set up a separate command—elevated title is not enough to aid strength; in plain truth, how can one add mutual harm?
translations.idiomatic: To carve off yet another command from the great headquarters and set up a separate colonel's office—an exalted title will not make the region stronger; in plain truth, how can splitting authority do anything but weaken it?

sentences.zh: 且資力旣分，職司增廣，衆勞務倍，文案滋煩。

translations.literal: Moreover, once resources and strength are divided, offices and duties multiply, the people's labor doubles, and paperwork grows ever more burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: Once resources and manpower are divided, offices and duties multiply, the people's burdens double, and paperwork becomes ever more oppressive.

sentences.zh: 非獨臣見其難，竊以爲國計非允。」

translations.literal: It is not only that your servant sees the difficulty; I venture to think the state's plan is not fitting."
translations.idiomatic: It is not only that your servant foresees the difficulty—I venture to believe the plan ill serves the state."

sentences.zh: 見許。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 於是罷南蠻校尉官。

translations.literal: Thereupon the office of Colonel of the Southern Barbarians was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The post of Colonel of the Southern Barbarians was accordingly abolished.

sentences.zh: 進號前將軍。

translations.literal: His designation was advanced to General of the Van.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced in rank to General of the Van.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，徵右僕射。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Huan was summoned as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu ascended the throne, Huan was recalled as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 仍轉使持節監湘州軍事、前將軍、湘州刺史，

translations.literal: He was then transferred as bearer of the staff of authority supervising military affairs in Xiang Province, General of the Van, and Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to bearer of the staff of authority supervising military affairs in Xiang Province, with the ranks of General of the Van and Governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，徙爲散騎常侍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming, he was moved to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Governor of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongming, he was then transferred to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Governor of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 初省江州軍府。

translations.literal: For the first time the military headquarters of Jiang Province was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion the military headquarters of Jiang Province was abolished for the first time.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷右僕射，本州中正。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was moved to Right Vice Director and became the provincial rectifier of his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Right Vice Director and provincial rectifier for his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 奐無學術，以事幹見處。

translations.literal: Huan had no scholarly learning but was placed in office because of his practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: Huan had no scholarly training but was advanced on account of his executive talent.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書僕射，中正如故。

translations.literal: He was moved to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; his rectifier post was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat while retaining his post as rectifier.

sentences.zh: 校籍郎王植屬吏部郎孔琇之以校籍令史俞公喜求進署，矯稱奐意，植坐免官。

translations.literal: The registrar Wang Zhi, subordinate to the Ministry of Personnel Gentleman Kong Xiuzhi, had the registrar clerk Yu Gongxi seek an advancement posting while falsely claiming Huan's approval; Zhi was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The registrar Wang Zhi, acting under Ministry of Personnel Gentleman Kong Xiuzhi, had registrar clerk Yu Gongxi seek a promotion while falsely invoking Huan's authority; Zhi was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷散騎常侍，領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was moved to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 奐欲請車駕幸府。

translations.literal: Huan wished to request that the imperial carriage visit his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Huan wished to invite the emperor to visit his residence.

sentences.zh: 上晚信佛法，御膳不宰牲。

translations.literal: The emperor in his later years believed in Buddhism; the imperial meals did not slaughter animals.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the emperor had come to believe in Buddhism and would not have animals slaughtered for the imperial table.

sentences.zh: 使王晏謂奐曰：「吾前去年爲斷殺事，不復幸詣大臣已判，無容欻爾也。」

translations.literal: He had Wang Yan tell Huan: "I have already, these past years, ceased killing for food and no longer visit the homes of great ministers; the matter is settled—there is no room for a sudden change."
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Yan to tell Huan, "These past years I have given up slaughter for my meals and no longer visit the homes of high ministers; that policy is fixed—there is no room for a sudden exception."

sentences.zh: 王儉卒，上用奐爲尚書令，以問王晏。

translations.literal: When Wang Jian died, the emperor wished to use Huan as Director of the Imperial Secretariat and consulted Wang Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jian died, the emperor wished to appoint Huan Director of the Imperial Secretariat and asked Wang Yan's opinion.

sentences.zh: 晏位遇已重，與奐不能相推，答上曰：「柳世隆有重望，恐不宜在奐後。」

translations.literal: Yan's position and favor were already weighty, and he and Huan could not defer to each other; he answered the emperor: "Liu Shilong enjoys great prestige—I fear it would not be fitting to place him after Huan."
translations.idiomatic: Yan's standing was already great, and he and Huan could not readily yield to each other; he answered, "Liu Shilong commands great prestige—it would hardly be fitting to rank him below Huan."

sentences.zh: 乃轉爲左僕射，加給事中，出爲使持節、散騎常侍、都督雍梁南北秦四州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡軍事、鎮北將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He was therefore transferred to Left Vice Director, with the added post of Attendant Within the Gates, and sent out as bearer of the staff of authority, Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, commander of military affairs in Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, Southern Qin, Jingling in Jing Province, and Suixiang in Si Province, General Who Guards the North, and Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was therefore made Left Vice Director with the added post of Attendant Within the Gates, then sent out as bearer of the staff of authority, Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, commander of military affairs in Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, Southern Qin, Jingling in Jing Province, and Suixiang in Si Province, General Who Guards the North, and Governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 上謂王晏曰：「奐於釋氏，實自專至。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Wang Yan: "Huan's devotion to the Buddhist teaching is in truth extreme.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Wang Yan, "Huan's devotion to Buddhism is truly excessive.

sentences.zh: 其在鎮或以此妨務，卿相見言次及之，勿道吾意也。」

translations.literal: In his province he may let this hinder affairs; when you meet, bring it up in passing—do not say it is my idea."
translations.idiomatic: In his province he may let it interfere with his duties; when you see him, mention it in passing—but do not say it came from me."

sentences.zh: 上以行北諸戍士卒多襤縷，送褶三千具，令奐分賦之。

translations.literal: Because the garrison soldiers on the northern marches were mostly in rags, the emperor sent three thousand pairs of trousers and had Huan distribute them.
translations.idiomatic: Because the garrison troops on the northern marches were mostly in rags, the emperor sent three thousand pairs of trousers for Huan to distribute among them.

sentences.zh: 十一年，奐輙殺寧蠻長史劉興祖，上大怒，使御史中丞孔稚珪奏其事曰：

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Huan on his own authority killed Liu Xingzu, chief administrator of the Pacification of the Barbarians; the emperor was greatly angered and had the Imperial Censor Kong Zhigui memorialize the case, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Huan killed on his own authority Liu Xingzu, chief administrator of the Pacification of the Barbarians. The emperor was furious and ordered Imperial Censor Kong Zhigui to memorialize the case as follows:

sentences.zh: :　　雍州刺史王奐啓錄小府長史劉興祖，虛稱「興祖扇動山蠻，規生逆謀，誑言誹謗，言辭不遜」。

translations.literal: Governor of Yong Province Wang Huan reported and arrested the minor headquarters chief administrator Liu Xingzu, falsely alleging: "Xingzu has stirred up the mountain barbarians, plotted rebellion, spread deceitful slander, and used insubordinate language."
translations.idiomatic: The Governor of Yong Province, Wang Huan, reported and had arrested his minor headquarters chief administrator Liu Xingzu, falsely charging that "Xingzu has incited the mountain barbarians, plotted rebellion, spread slanderous falsehoods, and spoken insubordinately."

sentences.zh: 敕使送興祖下都，奐慮所啓欺妄，於獄打殺興祖，詐啓稱自經死。

translations.literal: An imperial order directed that Xingzu be sent down to the capital; Huan, fearing that his report would be exposed as false, beat Xingzu to death in prison and falsely reported that he had hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order directed that Xingzu be sent to the capital; fearing that his report would be exposed as false, Huan beat him to death in prison and falsely reported that he had hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 止今體傷楗蒼，事暴聞聽。

translations.literal: Even now the wounds on the body are plain; the matter has burst upon the court's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Even now the wounds on the body are plain for all to see, and the affair has come to the court's attention.

sentences.zh: :　　攝興祖門生劉倪到臺辨問，列「興祖與奐共事，不能相和。

translations.literal: Liu Ni, a student of Xingzu, was brought to the capital for examination and stated: "Xingzu and Huan served together but could not get along.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzu's student Liu Ni was brought to the capital for questioning and testified that "Xingzu and Huan served together but could not get along.

sentences.zh: 自去年朱公恩領軍征蠻失利，興祖啓聞，以啓呈奐，奐因此便相嫌恨。

translations.literal: Since last year Zhu Gong'en led troops against the barbarians and suffered defeat, Xingzu reported it and presented the report to Huan; Huan therefore came to bear hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Last year Zhu Gong'en led a campaign against the barbarians and met defeat; Xingzu reported this and presented the report to Huan, who thereafter bore him a grudge.

sentences.zh: 若云興祖有罪，便應事在民間；

translations.literal: If one says Xingzu was guilty, the matter ought to have been among the people;
translations.idiomatic: If Xingzu were truly guilty, the matter should have been known among the people;

sentences.zh: 民間恬然，都無事迹。

translations.literal: among the people all was tranquil and there were no facts at all.
translations.idiomatic: yet among the people all was calm and no such facts existed.

sentences.zh: 去十年九月十八日，奐使仗身三十人來，稱敕錄興祖付獄。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day of the ninth month of the tenth year past, Huan sent thirty armed attendants who claimed an imperial order to arrest Xingzu and hand him to prison.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth day of the ninth month two years ago, Huan sent thirty armed attendants who claimed an imperial order to arrest Xingzu and commit him to prison.

sentences.zh: 安定郡蠻先在郡贓私，興祖旣知其取與，卽牒啓，奐不問。

translations.literal: A barbarian of Anding Commandery had earlier committed private graft in the commandery; Xingzu, knowing his takings and payments, immediately submitted a written report, but Huan made no inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: A barbarian of Anding Commandery had earlier committed private graft in the prefecture; Xingzu, knowing the details of his bribes, at once submitted a written report, but Huan made no inquiry.

sentences.zh: 興祖後執錄，奐仍令蠻領仗身於獄守視。

translations.literal: After Xingzu was arrested, Huan still had the barbarian lead armed attendants to guard and watch him in prison.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingzu was arrested, Huan still had that barbarian lead armed attendants to guard him in prison.

sentences.zh: 興祖未死之前，於獄以物畫漆柈子中出密報家，道無罪，令啓乞出都一辨，萬死無恨」。

translations.literal: Before Xingzu died, in prison he used an object to draw on a lacquered tray and sent a secret message to his family, saying he was innocent and asking them to petition that he be brought to the capital for a hearing—he would die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Before he died, Xingzu scratched a secret message on a lacquered tray in prison and sent it to his family, declaring his innocence and asking them to petition that he be brought to the capital for a hearing—he would accept any punishment without regret."

sentences.zh: 又云：「奐駐興祖嚴禁信使，欲作方便，殺以除口舌。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Huan stationed strict guards on Xingzu and cut off messengers, intending to find an opportunity to kill him and silence his mouth."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Huan placed Xingzu under strict guard and cut off messengers, intending to seize an opportunity to kill him and silence him."

sentences.zh: 又云：「奐意乃可。

translations.literal: He also said: "Huan's intent was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "That was indeed Huan's intent.

sentences.zh: 奐第三息彪隨奐在州，凡事是非皆干豫，扇構密除興祖。」

translations.literal: Huan's third son Biao accompanied Huan in the province; in every matter of right and wrong he intervened, inciting plots to have Xingzu secretly removed."
translations.idiomatic: Huan's third son Biao was with him in the province and meddled in every decision, inciting plots to have Xingzu secretly eliminated."

sentences.zh: 又云：「興祖家餉糜，中下藥，食兩口便覺，回乞獄子，食者皆大利。

translations.literal: He also said: "Xingzu's family sent gruel; poison was placed in it—after two mouthfuls he felt ill and begged the jailer; all who ate it suffered severely.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Xingzu's family sent gruel in which poison had been placed; after two mouthfuls he fell ill and begged the jailer—everyone who ate of it was violently purged.

sentences.zh: 興祖大呌道『糜中有藥』。

translations.literal: Xingzu cried out loudly: 'There is poison in the gruel.'
translations.idiomatic: Xingzu cried out, 'There is poison in the gruel!'

sentences.zh: 近獄之家，無人不聞。」

translations.literal: Among families near the prison, there was none who did not hear."
translations.idiomatic: Every household near the prison heard it."

sentences.zh: 又云：「奐治著興祖日急，判無濟理。

translations.literal: He also said: "Huan's handling of Xingzu grew more pressing day by day; plainly there was no hope of deliverance.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Huan pressed Xingzu harder day by day; plainly there was no hope of survival.

sentences.zh: 十一月二十一日，奐使獄吏來報興祖家，道興祖於獄自經死。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of the eleventh month, Huan sent prison clerks to report to Xingzu's family that Xingzu had hanged himself in prison.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day of the eleventh month, Huan sent prison clerks to tell Xingzu's family that he had hanged himself in prison.

sentences.zh: 尸出，家人共洗浴之，見興祖頸下有傷，肩胛烏，陰下破碎，實非興祖自經死。

translations.literal: When the corpse was brought out, the family together washed the body and saw wounds beneath Xingzu's neck, blackened shoulders, and shattered private parts—truly he had not hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the body was brought out, the family washed it together and found wounds on the neck, blackened shoulders, and shattered private parts—clearly he had not died by hanging.

sentences.zh: 家人及門義共見，非是一人。」

translations.literal: Family and retainers all saw it; it was not a single person."
translations.idiomatic: Family and retainers alike witnessed it—many people, not one alone."

sentences.zh: 重攝檢雍州都留田文喜，列與倪符同狀。

translations.literal: Tian Wenxi, who had remained in Yong Province, was again taken for examination; his statements matched Ni's in every particular.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Wenxi, who had remained in Yong Province, was examined again; his testimony matched Ni's in every detail.

sentences.zh: :　　興祖在獄，嗛苦望下，旣蒙降旨，欣願始遂，豈容於此，方復自經？

translations.literal: Xingzu in prison endured bitter hardship while looking to the court; having received the gracious decree, his glad hope was just fulfilled—how could he at this moment hang himself again?
translations.idiomatic: Xingzu in prison had suffered bitterly while awaiting the court's mercy; having received the gracious decree, his long hope was at last fulfilled—how could he at that moment take his own life?

sentences.zh: 敕以十九日至，興祖以二十一日死，推理檢迹，灼然矯假。

translations.literal: The decree arrived on the nineteenth; Xingzu died on the twenty-first—reasoning through the evidence, the forgery is glaringly clear.
translations.idiomatic: The decree arrived on the nineteenth and Xingzu died on the twenty-first; weighed by reason and evidence, the fraud is glaringly clear.

sentences.zh: 尋敕使送下，奐輙拒詔，所謗諸條，悉出奐意。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter an imperial messenger was to escort him down; Huan abruptly defied the decree. Every item of slander issued entirely from Huan's intent.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial messenger was shortly to escort him to the capital, yet Huan defied the decree. Every charge of slander came entirely from Huan's own design.

sentences.zh: 毀故丞相若陳顯達，誹訕朝事，莫此之深。

translations.literal: He slandered the late Chancellor Chen Xianda and reviled court affairs—nothing goes deeper.
translations.idiomatic: He slandered the late Chancellor Chen Xianda and reviled the court—nothing could be more grave.

sentences.zh: 彪私隨父之鎮，敢亂王法，罪竝合窮戮。

translations.literal: Biao privately followed his father to the province and dared to disturb royal law; his crime together warrants the utmost punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Biao had followed his father to the province without authorization and dared to violate the law—his crimes together warrant the utmost penalty.

sentences.zh: 上遣中書舍人呂文顯、直閤將軍曹道剛領齋仗五百人收奐。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Palace Gentlemen Lu Wenxian and the Direct Gate General Cao Daogang leading five hundred palace guards to take Huan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Palace Gentleman Lu Wenxian and Direct Gate General Cao Daogang with five hundred palace guards to arrest Huan.

sentences.zh: 敕鎮西司馬曹虎從江陵步道會襄陽。

translations.literal: He ordered the General Who Guards the West's chief administrator Cao Hu to march overland from Jiangling and join forces at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Chief Administrator Cao Hu of the General Who Guards the West to march overland from Jiangling and rendezvous at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 奐子彪素凶剽，奐不能制。

translations.literal: Huan's son Biao was by nature fierce and violent; Huan could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's son Biao had always been fierce and violent, and Huan could not control him.

sentences.zh: 女婿殷叡懼禍，謂奐曰：「曹、呂今來，旣不見真敕，恐爲姦變，政宜錄取，馳啓聞耳。」

translations.literal: His son-in-law Yin Rui, fearing disaster, said to Huan: "Cao and Lu have come now without showing the true decree—I fear a treacherous turn; you should just arrest them and send a swift report."
translations.idiomatic: His son-in-law Yin Rui, fearing disaster, said to Huan, "Cao and Lu have come without showing the true decree—I fear treachery; you should arrest them at once and send an urgent report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 奐納之。

translations.literal: Huan accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Huan accepted the advice.

sentences.zh: 彪輙令率州內得千餘人，開鎮庫，取仗，配衣甲，出南堂陳兵，閉門拒守。

translations.literal: Biao on his own authority mustered more than a thousand men within the province, opened the headquarters arsenal, took weapons, issued armor, deployed troops in the southern hall, closed the gates, and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Biao at once mustered more than a thousand men in the province, opened the headquarters arsenal, issued arms and armor, drew up troops in the southern hall, closed the gates, and prepared to resist.

sentences.zh: 奐門生鄭羽叩頭啓奐，乞出城迎臺使。

translations.literal: Huan's student Zheng Yu kowtowed and petitioned Huan, begging to go out of the city to welcome the capital envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's student Zheng Yu kowtowed and begged Huan to go out and welcome the envoys from the capital.

sentences.zh: 奐曰：「我不作賊，欲先遣啓自申。

translations.literal: Huan said: "I am not becoming a rebel; I wish first to send a report to explain myself.
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "I am no rebel; I wish first to send a memorial in my own defense.

sentences.zh: 政恐曹、呂輩小人相陵藉，故且閉門自守耳。」

translations.literal: I only fear that Cao, Lu, and such petty men will bully and trample us—therefore for the moment I close the gates and hold my own."
translations.idiomatic: I only fear that petty men like Cao and Lu will abuse us—so for the moment I close the gates and hold my ground."

sentences.zh: 彪遂出與虎軍戰，其黨范虎領二百人降臺軍，彪敗走歸。

translations.literal: Biao then went out to fight Hu's army; his follower Fan Hu led two hundred men in surrender to the capital forces, and Biao was defeated and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Biao then went out to fight Hu's army; his follower Fan Hu led two hundred men over to the capital forces, and Biao was beaten and fled back inside.

sentences.zh: 土人起義攻州西門，彪登門拒戰，却之。

translations.literal: Local men rose in arms and attacked the western gate of the province; Biao mounted the gate to resist and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Local men rose and attacked the western gate of the headquarters; Biao mounted the gate to fight them off and repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 奐司馬黃瑤起、寧蠻長史裴叔業於城內起兵攻奐。

translations.literal: Huan's chief administrator Huang Yaoqi and the chief administrator of the Pacification of the Barbarians Pei Shuye raised troops within the city to attack Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's chief administrator Huang Yaoqi and Pei Shuye, chief administrator of the Pacification of the Barbarians, raised troops inside the city to attack him.

sentences.zh: 奐聞兵入，還內禮佛，未及起，軍人遂斬之。

translations.literal: Huan, hearing troops enter, returned inside to worship the Buddha; before he could rise, the soldiers cut him down.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that troops had entered, Huan went inside to worship the Buddha; before he could rise, the soldiers cut him down.

sentences.zh: 年五十九。

translations.literal: He was fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-nine years old.

sentences.zh: 執彪及弟爽、弼、殷叡，皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Biao and his brothers Shuang and Bi were seized, together with Yin Rui; all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Biao, his brothers Shuang and Bi, and Yin Rui were seized and all put to death.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「逆賊王奐，險詖之性，自少及長。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The rebel Wang Huan has a treacherous and perverse nature from youth to age.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "The rebel Wang Huan has been treacherous and perverse from youth to age.

sentences.zh: 外飾廉勤，內懷凶慝，貽戾郷伍，取棄衣冠。

translations.literal: Outwardly he adorned himself with frugality and diligence; inwardly he harbored fierce malice, bringing offense to his township and rejection by the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he affected frugality and diligence; inwardly he harbored fierce malice, offending his neighbors and earning the contempt of the gentry.

sentences.zh: 拔其文筆之用，擢以顯任，出牧樊阿，政刑弛亂。

translations.literal: He was plucked for his literary and clerical skill and promoted to conspicuous office; sent out to govern Fan'e, his government and punishments were lax and chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted for his clerical skill to conspicuous office and sent to govern Fan'e, where government and punishments fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 第三息彪矯弄威權，父子均勢。

translations.literal: His third son Biao arrogantly wielded authority; father and son shared equal power.
translations.idiomatic: His third son Biao arrogantly wielded power as though father and son were equals.

sentences.zh: 故寧蠻長史劉興祖忠於奉國，每事匡執，奐忿其異己，誣以訕謗，肆怒囚錄，然後奏聞。

translations.literal: The former chief administrator of the Pacification of the Barbarians Liu Xingzu was loyal in serving the state and in every matter held firm to correct him; Huan resented his dissent, falsely charged him with slander, in rage imprisoned and recorded him, and only then reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: The former chief administrator of the Pacification of the Barbarians, Liu Xingzu, had been loyal in state service and steadfastly corrected him in every matter; Huan resented his independence, falsely charged him with slander, in rage had him imprisoned, and only then reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 朕察奐愚詐，詔送興祖還都，乃懼姦謀發露，潛加殺害。

translations.literal: We perceived Huan's foolish deceit and decreed that Xingzu be sent back to the capital; then, fearing exposure of his wicked plot, he secretly added murder.
translations.idiomatic: We perceived Huan's foolish deceit and ordered Xingzu sent back to the capital; then, fearing that his plot would be exposed, he secretly had him killed.

sentences.zh: 欺罔旣彰，中使辯覈，遂授兵登陴，逆捍王命。

translations.literal: Once the deception was manifest and the imperial messenger came to examine the case, he then handed out weapons, mounted the walls, and defied the royal command.
translations.idiomatic: When the deception was exposed and the imperial messenger came to investigate, he armed his men, mounted the walls, and defied the royal command.

sentences.zh: 天威電掃，義夫咸奮，曾未浹辰，罪人斯獲，方隅克殄，漢南肅清。

translations.literal: Heaven's majesty swept like lightning, righteous men all roused themselves; before a full ten days had passed the guilty were taken, the regions were extinguished, and south of the Han was made serene.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's wrath swept like lightning and loyal men rose as one; in less than ten days the culprits were seized, the rebel regions subdued, and the lands south of the Han restored to order.

sentences.zh: 自非犯官兼預同逆謀，爲一時所驅逼者，悉無所問。」

translations.literal: Except for officials who both shared in the same treasonous plot, all who were driven by the moment are not to be questioned."
translations.idiomatic: Except for officials who took part in the conspiracy itself, all who were merely driven by the moment shall go unpunished."

sentences.zh: 奐長子太子中庶子融，融弟司徒從事中郎琛，於都棄市。

translations.literal: Huan's eldest son Rong, Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household, and Rong's younger brother Chen, Attendant in the Secretariat, were exposed in the market at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's eldest son Rong, Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household, and Rong's younger brother Chen, Attendant in the Secretariat, were executed in the market at the capital.

sentences.zh: 餘孫皆原宥。

translations.literal: The remaining grandsons were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining grandsons were all granted pardon.

sentences.zh: 殷叡

translations.literal: Yin Rui
translations.idiomatic: Yin Rui

sentences.zh: =殷叡字文子，陳郡人。

translations.literal: Yin Rui, style name Wenzi, was a native of Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Rui, whose style name was Wenzi, came from Chen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 晉太常融七世孫也。

translations.literal: He was the seventh-generation descendant of Rong, Minister of Ceremonies in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was the seventh-generation descendant of Rong, Minister of Ceremonies under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉末，祖元素坐染太初事誅。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia in Song, his grandfather Yuansu was executed for involvement in the Taichu affair.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanjia era in Song, his grandfather Yuansu was executed for involvement in the Taichu affair.

sentences.zh: 叡遺腹亦當從戮，外曾祖王僧朗啓孝武救之，得免。

translations.literal: Rui, still in the womb, was also to be put to death with the clan; his great-grandfather by marriage Wang Senglang petitioned Emperor Xiaowu to save him, and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Rui, still in the womb, was also marked for execution; his great-grandfather by marriage Wang Senglang petitioned Emperor Xiaowu on his behalf, and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 叡解文義，有口才，司徒褚淵甚重之，謂之曰：「諸殷自荊州以來，無出卿右者。」

translations.literal: Rui understood literary meaning and had a gift for speech; Minister of Works Chu Yuan greatly valued him and said to him: "Among the Yin clan since Jing Province, none has surpassed you."
translations.idiomatic: Rui was versed in literary learning and gifted in speech; Minister of Works Chu Yuan held him in high regard and said, "Among the Yin family since the Jingzhou branch, none has surpassed you.

sentences.zh: 叡歛容答曰：「殷族衰悴，誠不如昔，若此旨爲虛，故不足降；

translations.literal: Rui composed his countenance and answered: "The Yin clan has declined and withered—it is truly not as in former days. If this intent is empty, it is therefore not worth lowering;
translations.idiomatic: Rui composed his expression and replied, "The Yin clan has declined and is truly not what it once was. If your words are mere flattery, they are not worth answering;

sentences.zh: 此旨爲實，彌不可聞。」

translations.literal: if this intent is real, it is all the more unbearable to hear."
translations.idiomatic: if they are true, they are all the more painful to hear."

sentences.zh: 奐爲雍州，啓叡爲府長史。

translations.literal: When Huan was in Yong Province, he recommended Rui as chief administrator of his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan governed Yong Province, he recommended Rui as chief administrator of his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 叡族父恒，字昭度，與叡同承融後。

translations.literal: Rui's clansman uncle Heng, style name Zhaodu, with Rui alike succeeded to Rong's line.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's clansman uncle Heng, whose style name was Zhaodu, like Rui succeeded to Rong's line.

sentences.zh: 宋司空景仁孫也。

translations.literal: He was grandson of Jingren, Minister of Works in Song.
translations.idiomatic: He was the grandson of Jingren, Minister of Works in the Song.

sentences.zh: 恒及父道矜，竝有古風，以是見蚩於世，其事非一。

translations.literal: Heng and his father Daojin both had an antique manner; for this they were mocked by the world—not a single instance alone.
translations.idiomatic: Heng and his father Daojin both affected an antique manner, for which they were ridiculed in their day on more than one occasion.

sentences.zh: 恒，宋泰始初，爲度支尚書，坐屬父疾及身疾多，爲有司所奏。

translations.literal: Heng, at the beginning of Taishi in Song, was Minister of Revenue; he was impeached because his father's illness and his own frequent illnesses fell under the statute.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taishi era in Song, Heng served as Minister of Revenue but was impeached because his father's illness and his own frequent illnesses violated regulations on mourning and attendance.

sentences.zh: 明帝詔曰：「殷道矜有生便病，比更無橫病。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming's edict said: "Yin Daojin has been ill from birth; recently there has been no sudden illness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming's edict read, "Yin Daojin has been ill from birth; recently he has suffered no sudden illness.

sentences.zh: 恒因愚習惰，久妨清敘。

translations.literal: Heng, through foolish habit and sloth, has long obstructed clear advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Heng, through foolish habit and sloth, has long obstructed proper advancement in office.

sentences.zh: 左遷散騎常侍，領校尉。」

translations.literal: He is demoted to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and concurrently Colonel."
translations.idiomatic: He is demoted to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and concurrently Colonel.

sentences.zh: 恒歷官清顯，至金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Heng passed through clear and eminent offices and reached Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.
translations.idiomatic: Heng nevertheless served through a series of eminent posts and rose to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.

sentences.zh: 建武中，卒。

translations.literal: During Jianwu he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Jianwu era.

sentences.zh: 奐弟女爲長沙王晃妃，世祖詔曰：「奐自陷逆節，長沙王妃男女竝長，且奐又出繼，前代或當有准，可特不離絕。」

translations.literal: Huan's younger sister's daughter was consort to Prince Huang of Changsha. Emperor Shizu's edict said: "Huan brought himself into treason; the Princess of Changsha's sons and daughters are both grown, and moreover Huan was given in adoption—former ages perhaps had precedents; they may specially not be severed."
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of Huan's younger sister was consort to Prince Huang of Changsha. Emperor Shizu decreed, "Huan brought treason upon himself, but the Princess of Changsha's children are grown, and Huan himself was given in adoption—precedents exist from earlier ages; their ties shall not be severed.

sentences.zh: 奐從弟繢。

translations.literal: Huan's cousin Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's cousin was Wang Hui.

sentences.zh: 奐從弟 繢

translations.literal: Huan's cousin Hui
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui, Huan's Cousin

sentences.zh: =繢字叔素，宋車騎將軍景文子也。

translations.literal: Hui, style name Shusu, was son of Jingwen, General of Chariots and Cavalry in Song.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui, whose style name was Shusu, was the son of Jingwen, General of Chariots and Cavalry in the Song.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，爲祕書郎，太子舍人，轉中書舍人。

translations.literal: At capped age he became Secretariat Gentleman, Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household, then transferred to Palace Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching manhood he served as Secretariat Gentleman and Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household, then was transferred to Palace Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 景文以此授超階，令繢經年乃受。

translations.literal: Jingwen on this account granted him a leap in rank, but had Hui wait a full year before accepting.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen would have granted him a leap in rank on this account, but made Hui wait a full year before accepting the appointment.

sentences.zh: 景文封江安侯，繢襲其本爵，爲始平縣五等男。

translations.literal: Jingwen was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiang'an; Hui inherited his original rank and became a fifth-grade baron of Shiping County.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen had been enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiang'an; Hui inherited his original noble rank and became a fifth-grade baron of Shiping County.

sentences.zh: 遷祕書丞，司徒右長史。

translations.literal: He was moved to Secretariat Assistant and Right Chief Administrator of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Secretariat Assistant and Right Chief Administrator of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 元徽末，除寧朔將軍、建平王征北長史、南東海太守，黃門郎，寧朔將軍、東陽太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhui he was appointed General of Pacifying the North, chief administrator to the General Who Campaigns North for Prince of Jianping, Grand Administrator of Southern Donghai, Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, General of Pacifying the North, and Grand Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanhui era he was appointed General of Pacifying the North, chief administrator to the General Who Campaigns North for the Prince of Jianping, and Grand Administrator of Southern Donghai, then Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, General of Pacifying the North, and Grand Administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 世祖爲撫軍，吏部尚書張岱選繢爲長史，呈選牒。

translations.literal: When Shizu was General Who Pacifies the Army, Minister of Personnel Zhang Dai selected Hui as chief administrator and presented the selection document.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu was General Who Pacifies the Army, Minister of Personnel Zhang Dai selected Hui as his chief administrator and presented the nomination.

sentences.zh: 太祖笑謂岱曰：「此可謂素望。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gao laughed and said to Dai: "This may be called long-standing repute."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao smiled and said to Dai, "This is what one calls a man of established reputation.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍，驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: He was moved to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 出補義興太守。

translations.literal: He went out to fill the post of Grand Administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Grand Administrator of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 輙錄郡吏陳伯喜付陽羨獄，欲殺之，縣令孔逭不知何罪，不受繢教，爲有司所奏，繢坐白衣領職。

translations.literal: He on his own authority arrested the commandery clerk Chen Boxi and sent him to prison in Yangxian, intending to kill him; the magistrate of the county Kong Huan did not know what the crime was and would not accept Hui's order; he was reported by the responsible offices, and Hui was punished by serving in office in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: He on his own authority arrested commandery clerk Chen Boxi and sent him to prison in Yangxian intending to kill him; County Magistrate Kong Huan, not knowing the charge, refused to obey Hui's order; the matter was reported to the authorities, and Hui was reduced to serving in plain clothes.

sentences.zh: 遷太子中庶子，領驍騎，轉長兼侍中。

translations.literal: He was moved to Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household, concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry, then transferred to Chief Concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household and concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry, then Chief Concurrent Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 世祖出射雉，繢信佛法，稱疾不從駕。

translations.literal: When Shizu went out to shoot pheasants, Hui, believing in Buddhism, claimed illness and did not follow the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu went out pheasant hunting, Hui, a devout Buddhist, pleaded illness and did not accompany the imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 轉左民尚書，以母老乞解職，改授寧朔將軍、大司馬長史、淮陵太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Left for the People; because his mother was old he begged to resign office and was reassigned as General of Pacifying the North, chief administrator to the Grand Marshal, and Grand Administrator of Huailing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of the Left for the People; citing his mother's age, he asked to resign and was reassigned as General of Pacifying the North, chief administrator to the Grand Marshal, and Grand Administrator of Huailing.

sentences.zh: 出爲宣城太守，秩中二千石，

translations.literal: He went out as Grand Administrator of Xuancheng, with salary of two thousand piculs at the middle grade.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Grand Administrator of Xuancheng at the middle two-thousand-picul rank.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，遷輔國將軍、太傅長史，不拜。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang, he was moved to General Who Assists the State and chief administrator to the Grand Tutor but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longchang, he was appointed General Who Assists the State and chief administrator to the Grand Tutor but declined the post.

sentences.zh: 仍爲冠軍將軍、豫章內史。

translations.literal: He was then made General Who Establishes Valor and Interior Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made General Who Establishes Valor and Interior Administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 進號征虜。

translations.literal: His designation was advanced to General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: His designation was raised to General Who Subdues the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 又坐事免官。

translations.literal: He again was dismissed from office because of an affair.
translations.idiomatic: He was again dismissed from office for an offense.

sentences.zh: 除冠軍將軍，司徒左長史，散騎常侍，隨王師。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Establishes Valor, Left Chief Administrator of the Minister of Works, Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and tutor to the Prince of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Establishes Valor, Left Chief Administrator of the Minister of Works, Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and tutor to the Prince of Sui.

sentences.zh: 除征虜將軍，驃騎長史，遷散騎常侍，太常。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Subdues the Barbarians and chief administrator to the General of Agile Cavalry, then moved to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Subdues the Barbarians and chief administrator to the General of Agile Cavalry, then promoted to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，卒。

translations.literal: In Yongyuan 1, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Yongyuan.

sentences.zh: 年五十三。

translations.literal: He was fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-three years old.

sentences.zh: 諡靖子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Jingzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Jingzi.

sentences.zh: 繢女適安陸王子敬，世祖寵子，

translations.literal: Hui's daughter was married to Zijing, Prince of Anlu, a favored son of Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's daughter married Zijing, Prince of Anlu, a favorite son of Emperor Shizu.

sentences.zh: 永明三年，納妃，脩外舅姑之敬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongming, when he took a consort, he showed the respect due to his wife's parents.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongming, when the prince took her as consort, he showed the full respect due to his wife's parents.

sentences.zh: 世祖遣文惠太子相隨往繢家置酒設樂，公卿皆冠冕而至，當世榮之。

translations.literal: Shizu sent the Crown Prince Wen Hui to accompany him in going to Hui's house to set out wine and music; dukes and ministers all came in caps and regalia—his age counted it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu sent Crown Prince Wen Hui to accompany the prince to Hui's house for a feast with music; dukes and ministers all came in full court dress—the age regarded it as the highest honor.

sentences.zh: 張沖

translations.literal: Zhang Chong
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong

sentences.zh: 張沖字思約，吳郡吳人。

translations.literal: Zhang Chong, style name Siyue, was a native of Wu in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong, whose style name was Siyue, came from Wu in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父柬，通直郎。

translations.literal: His father Jian was a Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jian had served as Direct Attendant.

sentences.zh: 沖出繼從伯侍中景胤，小名查，父邵，小名梨。

translations.literal: Chong was given in adoption to succeed his father's elder cousin, the Attendant Within Jingyin; his childhood name was Cha; his father Shao's childhood name was Li.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had been given in adoption to succeed his father's elder cousin Jingyin, Attendant Within; his childhood name was Cha, and his father Shao's childhood name was Li.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝戲景胤曰：「查何如梨。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Song jested with Jingyin: "How does Cha compare with Li?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Song teased Jingyin, "How does Cha compare with Li?

sentences.zh: 景胤答曰：「梨是百果之宗，查何敢及。」

translations.literal: Jingyin answered: "Li is the sovereign of the hundred fruits—how dare Cha compare?"
translations.idiomatic: Jingyin answered, "Li is the sovereign of all fruits—how could Cha presume to compare?"

sentences.zh: 沖亦少有至性，辟州主簿，隨從叔永爲將帥，除綏遠將軍、盱眙太守。

translations.literal: Chong also in youth had utmost filial nature; he was summoned as provincial chief clerk, followed his uncle Yong as a commander, and was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and Grand Administrator of Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Chong too showed exceptional filial devotion from youth; summoned as provincial chief clerk, he followed his uncle Yong on campaign and was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and Grand Administrator of Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 永征彭城，遇寒雪，軍人足脛凍斷者十七八，沖足指皆墮。

translations.literal: When Yong campaigned at Pengcheng they met cold snow; seven or eight tenths of the soldiers had calves and shins frozen off; Chong's toes all fell off.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong campaigned at Pengcheng they met bitter cold and snow; seven or eight soldiers in ten suffered frozen calves and shins, and Chong lost all his toes.

sentences.zh: 除尚書駕部郎，桂陽王征南中兵，振威將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman of the Imperial Carriages in the Secretariat, central army officer for the Campaign South of Prince Guiyang, and General Who Inspires Awe.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Gentleman of the Imperial Carriages in the Secretariat, central army officer on the southern campaign of the Prince of Guiyang, and General Who Inspires Awe.

sentences.zh: 歷驃騎太尉南中郎參軍，不拜。

translations.literal: He passed through service as aide in the Southern Palace of the General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Marshal but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered a post as aide in the Southern Palace of the General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Marshal but declined.

sentences.zh: 遷征西從事中郎，通直郎，武陵王北中郎直兵參軍，長水校尉，除寧朔將軍，本官如故。

translations.literal: He was moved to Attendant in the Western Campaign, Direct Attendant, direct military aide to the Northern Central Commander for Prince of Wuling, Colonel of the Long River, and appointed General of Pacifying the North with his former office unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Attendant in the Western Campaign, Direct Attendant, direct military aide to the Northern Central Commander for the Prince of Wuling, and Colonel of the Long River, then appointed General of Pacifying the North while retaining his former duties.

sentences.zh: 遷左軍將軍，加寧朔將軍，輔國將軍。

translations.literal: He was moved to General of the Left Army, with the added ranks General of Pacifying the North and General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Left Army, with the added ranks of General of Pacifying the North and General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 沖少從戎事，朝廷以幹力相待，故歷處軍校之官。

translations.literal: Chong from youth followed military affairs; the court treated him for practical ability, and therefore he passed through posts in military commands.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had followed military life from youth, and the court valued him for his practical ability, so he served in a succession of military commands.

sentences.zh: 出爲馬頭太守，徙盱眙太守，輔國將軍如故，

translations.literal: He went out as Grand Administrator of Matou, was moved to Grand Administrator of Xuyi, and his rank as General Who Assists the State was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Grand Administrator of Matou, then transferred to Grand Administrator of Xuyi, retaining his rank as General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 永明六年，遷西陽王冠軍司馬。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongming, he was moved to chief administrator to the Champion General for Prince of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yongming, he was then appointed chief administrator to the Champion General for the Prince of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 八年，爲假節、監青冀二州刺史事，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made provisional bearer of the staff of authority supervising affairs in Qing and Ji provinces; his generalship was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made provisional bearer of the staff of authority supervising Qing and Ji provinces, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 沖父初卒，遺命曰：「祭我必以郷土所產，無用牲物。」

translations.literal: When Chong's father first died, his testament said: "In sacrificing to me you must use products of the native land—do not use sacrificial animals."
translations.idiomatic: When Chong's father died, his last testament read, "Sacrifice to me only with produce of our native land—use no sacrificial animals.

sentences.zh: 沖在鎮，四時還吳園中取果菜，流涕薦焉。

translations.literal: While Chong was in his province, each season he returned to the garden in Wu to take fruit and vegetables and, weeping, offered them.
translations.idiomatic: While stationed in the provinces, Chong each season returned to the family garden in Wu to gather fruit and vegetables and, weeping, offered them in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 仍轉刺史。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to full governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed full governor.

sentences.zh: 鬱林卽位，進號冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yulin took the throne, Chong's designation was advanced to General Who Establishes Valor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yulin ascended the throne, Chong's designation was raised to General Who Establishes Valor.

sentences.zh: 明帝卽位，以晉壽太守王洪範代沖。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Wang Hongfan, Grand Administrator of Jinshou, was made to replace Chong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Wang Hongfan, Grand Administrator of Jinshou, was appointed to replace him.

sentences.zh: 除黃門郎，加征虜將軍，

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gate with the added rank General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gate with the added rank of General Who Subdues the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，虜寇淮泗，假沖節，都督青冀二州北討諸軍事，本官如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, when the barbarians raided Huai and Si, Chong was given provisional staff of authority as commander of all northern campaign forces in Qing and Ji provinces; his original office was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu, when the barbarians raided the Huai and Si region, Chong was given provisional staff of authority as commander of the northern campaign in Qing and Ji provinces, retaining his former title.

sentences.zh: 虜并兵攻司州，詔青徐出軍分其兵勢。

translations.literal: The barbarians combined forces to attack Si Province; an edict ordered Qing and Xu to send out troops to divide their military strength.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians massed their forces to attack Si Province, and an edict ordered troops from Qing and Xu to march out and divide the enemy's strength.

sentences.zh: 沖遣軍主桑係祖由渣口攻拔虜建陵、驛馬、厚丘三城，多所殺獲。

translations.literal: Chong sent the army commander Sang Xizu through Zhakou to attack and take the barbarian cities Jianling, Yima, and Houqiu, killing and capturing many.
translations.idiomatic: Chong sent army commander Sang Xizu through Zhakou to storm the enemy cities of Jianling, Yima, and Houqiu, killing and capturing many.

sentences.zh: 又與洪範遣軍主崔季延襲虜紀城，據之。

translations.literal: Together with Hongfan he also sent the army commander Cui Jiyan to raid the barbarian city of Jicheng and seize it.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Hongfan he sent army commander Cui Jiyan to raid the enemy city of Jicheng and hold it.

sentences.zh: 沖又遣軍主杜僧護攻拔虜虎坑、馮時、卽丘三城，驅生口輜重還，至溘溝，虜救兵至，緣道要擊，僧護力戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Chong again sent the army commander Du Senghu to attack and take the barbarian cities Hukeng, Fengshi, and Jiqiu, driving captives and baggage back; when they reached Keigou the barbarian relief troops arrived and lay in ambush along the road to strike; Senghu fought fiercely and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Chong also sent army commander Du Senghu to storm the enemy cities of Hukeng, Fengshi, and Jiqiu and drive back captives and baggage; at Keigou enemy relief troops lay in ambush along the road, but Senghu fought fiercely and routed them.

sentences.zh: 其年，遷廬陵王北中郎司馬、加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: That year he was moved to chief administrator to the Northern Central Commander for Prince of Luling, with the added rank General Who Establishes Valor.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was appointed chief administrator to the Northern Central Commander for the Prince of Luling, with the added rank of General Who Establishes Valor.

sentences.zh: 未拜，豐城公遙昌爲豫州，上慮寇難未已，徙沖爲征虜長史、南梁郡太守，

translations.literal: Before he took office, Duke of Fengcheng Yaochang became governor of Yu Province; the emperor, fearing that border troubles were not yet ended, moved Chong to chief administrator to the General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Grand Administrator of Nanliang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, the Duke of Fengcheng Yaochang was assigned to Yu Province; fearing that border troubles were not over, the emperor transferred Chong to chief administrator to the General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Grand Administrator of Nanliang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，除江夏王前軍長史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, he was appointed chief administrator of the Vanguard Army for the Prince of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai, he was then appointed chief administrator of the Vanguard Army for the Prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 東昏卽位，出爲建安王征虜長史、輔國將軍、江夏內史，行郢州府州事，

translations.literal: When Emperor Donghun took the throne, he went out as chief administrator to the General Who Subdues the Barbarians for Prince of Jian'an, General Who Assists the State, and Interior Administrator of Jiangxia, acting for the headquarters and province of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Donghun ascended the throne, he was sent out as chief administrator to the General Who Subdues the Barbarians for the Prince of Jian'an, General Who Assists the State, and Interior Administrator of Jiangxia, acting for the Ying provincial headquarters.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，遷持節、督豫州軍事、豫州刺史，代裴叔業。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan, he was moved to bearer of the staff of authority supervising military affairs in Yu Province and Governor of Yu Province, replacing Pei Shuye.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongyuan, he was transferred to bearer of the staff of authority supervising military affairs in Yu Province and Governor of Yu Province, to replace Pei Shuye.

sentences.zh: 竟不行。

translations.literal: In the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷督南兖兖徐青冀五州、輔國將軍、南兖州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: The next year he was moved to commander of Nan Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji provinces, General Who Assists the State, and Governor of Nan Yan Province, with staff of authority unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed commander of Nan Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji provinces, General Who Assists the State, and Governor of Nan Yan Province, retaining his staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 會司州刺史申希祖卒，以沖爲督司州軍事、冠軍將軍、司州刺史。

translations.literal: When Governor of Si Province Shen Xizu died, Chong was made commander of military affairs in Si Province, General Who Establishes Valor, and Governor of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor of Si Province Shen Xizu died, Chong was appointed commander of military affairs in Si Province, General Who Establishes Valor, and Governor of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 裴叔業以壽春降虜，又遷沖爲督南兖兖徐青冀五州、南兖州刺史，持節、將軍如故。

translations.literal: When Pei Shuye surrendered Shouchun to the barbarians, Chong was again moved to commander of Nan Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji provinces and Governor of Nan Yan Province, with staff of authority and generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Shuye surrendered Shouchun to the enemy, Chong was again appointed commander of Nan Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji provinces and Governor of Nan Yan Province, retaining his staff of authority and general's rank.

sentences.zh: 竝未拜。

translations.literal: He accepted none of these.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted none of these appointments.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景事平，徵建安王寶夤還都，以沖爲督郢司二州、郢州刺史，持節、將軍如故。

translations.literal: When Cui Huijing's affair was settled, Prince of Jian'an Bao Yin was recalled to the capital and Chong was made commander of Ying and Si provinces and Governor of Ying Province, with staff of authority and generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: After Cui Huijing's rebellion was suppressed, Prince Bao Yin of Jian'an was recalled to the capital and Chong was appointed commander of Ying and Si provinces and Governor of Ying Province, retaining his staff of authority and general's rank.

sentences.zh: 一歲之中，頻授四州，至此受任。

translations.literal: Within one year he was repeatedly given four provinces; only now did he accept appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single year he had been offered four provinces in succession; only now did he finally accept appointment.

sentences.zh: 其冬，進征虜將軍。

translations.literal: That winter his rank was advanced to General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was advanced to General Who Subdues the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 封定襄侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 梁王義師起，東昏遣驍騎將軍薛元嗣、制局監暨榮伯領兵及糧運百四十餘船送沖，使拒西師。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Liang's righteous army rose, Donghun sent the General of Valiant Cavalry Xue Yuansi and the Bureau Supervisor Ji Rongbo leading troops and more than a hundred and forty grain-transport ships to escort Chong and have him resist the western army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Liang's righteous army rose, Emperor Donghun sent General of Valiant Cavalry Xue Yuansi and Bureau Supervisor Ji Rongbo with troops and more than 140 grain transports to reinforce Chong and have him resist the western forces.

sentences.zh: 元嗣等懲劉山陽之敗，疑沖不敢進，停住夏口浦。

translations.literal: Yuansi and the others, mindful of Liu Shanyang's defeat, doubted that Chong dared advance and halted at Xiakou Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansi and his men, mindful of Liu Shanyang's defeat, doubted that Chong would dare advance and halted at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 聞義師將至，元嗣、榮伯相率入郢城。

translations.literal: Hearing that the righteous army was about to arrive, Yuansi and Rongbo together led their men into Ying city.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard that the righteous army was approaching, Yuansi and Rongbo led their forces into Ying city together.

sentences.zh: 時竟陵太守房僧寄被代還至郢，東昏敕僧寄留守魯山，除驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: At that time Fang Sengji, Grand Administrator of Jingling, having been replaced was returning and reached Ying; Donghun ordered Sengji to remain and hold Lushan and appointed him General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fang Sengji, Grand Administrator of Jingling, having been relieved of office, was on his way back and reached Ying; Donghun ordered him to hold Lushan and appointed him General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 僧寄謂沖曰：「臣雖未荷朝廷深恩，實蒙先帝厚澤。

translations.literal: Sengji said to Chong: "Your servant has not yet received the court's deep grace, but in truth I have enjoyed the former emperor's generous favor.
translations.idiomatic: Sengji said to Chong, "I have not yet received great favor from the present court, but I have indeed enjoyed the former emperor's generous grace.

sentences.zh: 蔭其樹者不折其枝，實欲微立塵效。」

translations.literal: One who enjoys the shade of a tree does not break its branches—I truly wish to set up a slight mark of dust-like service."
translations.idiomatic: One who enjoys the shade of a tree does not break its branches—I wish only to offer whatever small service I can.

sentences.zh: 沖深相許諾，共結盟誓。

translations.literal: Chong deeply pledged agreement with him and they jointly made a covenant oath.
translations.idiomatic: Chong gave him his solemn pledge, and the two of them swore a joint oath.

sentences.zh: 乃分部拒守。

translations.literal: Thereupon they divided their forces to resist and hold.
translations.idiomatic: They then divided their forces to organize the defense.

sentences.zh: 遣軍主孫樂祖數千人助僧寄據魯山岸立城壘。

translations.literal: He sent the army commander Sun Lezu with several thousand men to help Sengji hold Lushan, building ramparts on the bank.
translations.idiomatic: He sent army commander Sun Lezu with several thousand men to help Sengji hold Lushan and build fortifications along the shore.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，梁王出沔口，圍魯山城。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year the Prince of Liang came out from Hankou and besieged Lushan city.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year the Prince of Liang marched out from Hankou and besieged Lushan.

sentences.zh: 遣軍主曹景宗等過江攻郢城，未及盡濟，沖遣中兵參軍陳光靜等開門出擊，爲義師所破，光靜戰死，沖固守不出。

translations.literal: He sent the army commanders Cao Jingzong and others across the river to attack Ying city; before all had crossed, Chong sent the central army aide Chen Guangjing and others to open the gates and strike out; they were defeated by the righteous army, Guangjing died in battle, and Chong held firm and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: He sent army commanders including Cao Jingzong across the river to attack Ying; before the crossing was complete, Chong sent central army aide Chen Guangjing and others out through the gates to attack; the righteous army defeated them and Guangjing was killed in battle, after which Chong held the city and refused to come out.

sentences.zh: 景宗於是據石橋浦，連軍相續，下至加湖。

translations.literal: Jingzong thereupon took Shiqiao Ford, linking camps in succession down to Jiahu.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong thereupon occupied Shiqiao Ford and extended his camps in a continuous line down to Jiahu.

sentences.zh: 東昏遣軍主巴西梓潼二郡太守吳子陽、光子衿、李文釗、陳虎牙等十三軍援郢，至加湖不得進，乃築城舉烽，城內亦舉火應之。

translations.literal: Donghun sent the army commanders Wu Ziyang, Grand Administrator of the two commanderies Baxi and Zitong, Guang Zijin, Li Wenzhao, Chen Huya, and others with thirteen armies to relieve Ying; reaching Jiahu they could not advance, so they built a fort and raised beacon fires, and within the city fires were also raised in answer.
translations.idiomatic: Donghun sent army commanders including Wu Ziyang, Grand Administrator of Baxi and Zitong commanderies, Guang Zijin, Li Wenzhao, and Chen Huya with thirteen armies to relieve Ying; at Jiahu they could advance no farther and built a fortified camp with beacon fires, which the besieged answered with signal fires of their own.

sentences.zh: 而內外各自保，不能相救。

translations.literal: Yet inside and outside each held their own ground and could not rescue one another.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the forces inside and outside each held their own positions and could not aid one another.

sentences.zh: 沖病死，元嗣、榮伯與沖子孜及長史江夏內史程茂固守。

translations.literal: Chong died of illness; Yuansi, Rongbo, Chong's son Zi, and the chief administrator and Interior Administrator of Jiangxia Cheng Mao held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Chong died of illness; Yuansi, Rongbo, Chong's son Zi, and chief administrator Cheng Mao, who was also Interior Administrator of Jiangxia, continued to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 東昏詔贈沖散騎常侍、護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Donghun's edict posthumously awarded Chong Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Donghun posthumously awarded Chong the ranks of Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 假元嗣子陽節。

translations.literal: Yuansi was given provisional staff of authority as Ziyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansi was granted provisional staff of authority under the title Ziyang.

sentences.zh: 江水暴長，加湖城淹漬，義師乘高艦攻之，子陽等大敗散。

translations.literal: The river waters rose violently; the fort at Jiahu was inundated; the righteous army attacked from high ships, and Ziyang and the others were greatly defeated and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze rose in flood and the camp at Jiahu was inundated; the righteous army attacked from high-decked ships, and Ziyang's forces were routed and scattered.

sentences.zh: 魯山城乏糧，軍人於磯頭捕細魚供食，密治輕船，將奔夏口。

translations.literal: Lushan city lacked grain; soldiers at the stony foreshore caught small fish for food and secretly prepared light boats, intending to flee to Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan ran short of grain; the soldiers caught small fish on the stony shore to eat and secretly prepared light boats, intending to flee to Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 梁王命偏軍斷其取路，防備越逸。

translations.literal: The Prince of Liang ordered detached forces to cut off their escape routes and guard against their breaking out.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Liang ordered detached forces to cut off their escape routes and prevent any breakout.

sentences.zh: 房僧寄病死，孫樂祖窘，以城降。

translations.literal: Fang Sengji died of illness; Sun Lezu, pressed hard, surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Sengji died of illness; hard pressed, Sun Lezu surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 郢城被圍二百餘日，士庶病死者七八百家。

translations.literal: Ying city was besieged for more than two hundred days; among gentry and commoners, seven or eight hundred households had members who died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had been besieged for more than two hundred days; illness had killed members of seven or eight hundred gentry and commoner households.

sentences.zh: 魯山旣敗，程茂及元嗣等議降，使孜爲書與梁王。

translations.literal: Once Lushan had fallen, Cheng Mao and Yuansi and the others discussed surrender and had Zi write a letter to the Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: After Lushan fell, Cheng Mao, Yuansi, and the others discussed surrender and had Zi write to the Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 沖故吏青州治中房長瑜謂孜曰：「前使君忠貫昊天，操逾松竹。

translations.literal: Chong's former subordinate Fang Changyu, provincial aide of Qing Province, said to Zi: "The former envoy's loyalty pierced to heaven, his conduct surpassed pine and bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's former subordinate Fang Changyu, provincial aide of Qing Province, said to Zi, "Your father's loyalty reached to heaven, and his conduct surpassed pine and bamboo.

sentences.zh: 郎君但當端坐畫一，以荷析薪。

translations.literal: My lord need only sit upright and hold to one course, to bear the burden of splitting firewood.
translations.idiomatic: You need only hold firm to a single course and bear the burden your father laid upon you.

sentences.zh: 若天運不與，幅巾待命，以下從使君。

translations.literal: If heaven's fortune is not with you, put on plain cloth and await the command, then follow the envoy below.
translations.idiomatic: If heaven's fortune is not with you, dress in plain cloth and await your fate, then follow your father below.

sentences.zh: 今若隨諸人之計，非唯郢州士女失高山之望，亦恐彼所不取也。」

translations.literal: If now you follow the plans of these others, not only will the men and women of Ying Province lose their hope set on a high mountain—you also fear they will not accept it."
translations.idiomatic: If you now follow the others' plan, not only will the people of Ying lose the man they looked up to as a mountain—you may also find that the enemy will not accept you."

sentences.zh: 魯山陷後二日，元嗣等以郢城降。

translations.literal: Two days after Lushan fell, Yuansi and the others surrendered Ying city.
translations.idiomatic: Two days after Lushan fell, Yuansi and the others surrendered Ying.

sentences.zh: 東昏以程茂爲督郢司二州、輔國將軍、郢州刺史，元嗣爲督雍梁南北秦四州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡、冠軍將軍、雍州刺史，竝持節。

translations.literal: Donghun made Cheng Mao commander of Ying and Si provinces, General Who Assists the State, and Governor of Ying Province; Yuansi commander of Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, Southern Qin, Jingling in Jing Province, and Suixiang in Si Province, General Who Establishes Valor, and Governor of Yong Province—both bearing staffs of authority.
translations.idiomatic: Donghun appointed Cheng Mao commander of Ying and Si provinces, General Who Assists the State, and Governor of Ying Province, and Yuansi commander of Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, Southern Qin, Jingling in Jing Province, and Suixiang in Si Province, General Who Establishes Valor, and Governor of Yong Province—both with staffs of authority.

sentences.zh: 時郢魯二城已降，死者相積，竟無叛散。

translations.literal: At that time Ying and Lu had both surrendered; the dead lay heaped together, yet in the end there was no defection or scattering.
translations.idiomatic: By then both Ying and Lushan had fallen; the dead lay in heaps, yet there had been no mass desertion.

sentences.zh: 時以沖及房僧寄比臧洪之被圍也。

translations.literal: The age compared Chong and Fang Sengji to Zang Hong when he was besieged.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the day compared Chong and Fang Sengji to Zang Hong in his famous siege.

sentences.zh: 贈僧寄益州刺史。

translations.literal: Sengji was posthumously awarded the post of Governor of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Sengji was posthumously appointed Governor of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 時新蔡太守席謙，永明中爲中書郎王融所薦。

translations.literal: At that time Xi Qian, Grand Administrator of Xincai, had in the Yongming era been recommended by the Secretariat Gentleman Wang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xi Qian, Grand Administrator of Xincai, had been recommended in the Yongming era by Secretariat Gentleman Wang Rong.

sentences.zh: 父恭穆，鎮西司馬，爲魚復侯所害。

translations.literal: His father Gongmu, chief administrator to the General Who Guards the West, was killed by the Marquis of Yufu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gongmu, chief administrator to the General Who Guards the West, had been killed by the Marquis of Yufu.

sentences.zh: 至是謙鎮盆城，聞義師東下，曰：「我家世忠貞，殞死不二。」

translations.literal: At this time Qian held Pencheng; hearing that the righteous army was coming east, he said: "Our house for generations has been loyal and steadfast—death without a second thought."
translations.idiomatic: By then Qian was holding Pencheng; when he heard that the righteous army was marching east, he said, "Our house has been loyal for generations—I will die rather than turn."

sentences.zh: 爲陳伯之所殺。

translations.literal: He was killed by Chen Bozhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed by Chen Bozhi.

sentences.zh: 【史論】

translations.literal: [Historian's Appraisal]
translations.idiomatic: Historian's Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：石碏棄子，弘滅親之戒；

translations.literal: The historian says: Shi Que abandoned his son, magnifying the warning against destroying kin;
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Shi Que abandoned his son, setting forth the warning against destroying one's own kin;

sentences.zh: 鮑永晚降，知事新之節。

translations.literal: Bao Yong surrendered late, knowing the principle of serving the new.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yong surrendered late, showing the principle of serving the new order.

sentences.zh: 王奐誠在靡貳，迹允嚴科；

translations.literal: Wang Huan's loyalty was truly without duplicity, and his conduct fit the severe statute;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan's loyalty was truly without duplicity, and his conduct warranted the severe penalty;

sentences.zh: 張沖未達天心，守迷義運。

translations.literal: Zhang Chong did not comprehend heaven's heart and clung in delusion to a doomed cause.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong failed to read heaven's intent and clung stubbornly to a doomed cause.

sentences.zh: 致危之理異，爲亡之事一也。

translations.literal: The reasons that brought them to peril differed, but the matter of their ruin was one.
translations.idiomatic: The paths that led them into peril differed, but the outcome was the same.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：王居北牧，子未克家。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Wang held the northern pastures, but his son could not govern the household.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Wang ruled the northern marches, but his son could not keep the household in order.

sentences.zh: 終成干紀，覆此冑華。

translations.literal: In the end he accomplished rebellion against the norm and overturned this helmet's glory.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he committed rebellion and brought ruin on his noble house.

sentences.zh: 張壘窮守，死如亂麻。

translations.literal: Zhang's fortress was besieged to the end; death came like tangled hemp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's fortress was besieged to the end, and death came like tangled hemp.

sentences.zh: 爲悟旣晚，辯見方賒。

translations.literal: His awakening came too late; clear judgment had just been extended.
translations.idiomatic: His awakening came too late, and clear judgment only after the fact.

sentences.zh: 除青石疑

translations.literal: Removal of doubtful Qingstone variant readings.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note: removal of doubtful Qingstone variant readings.

sentences.zh: 案

translations.literal: Editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note.
